open_points: The source does not document any status-flag mechanism for the IDR access path, so no polling bound or error-return contract is specified beyond the absence of waiting.
The RM0486 section does not indicate whether CRC_IDR is readable during a halted CPU state, so whether the read-back verification applies while the CPU is halted is left open.

requirements.statement: While no LL function has been called after reset, the CRC LL driver shall not write any register.
requirements.verification: The test resets the CRC peripheral to its startup state and observes its registers; the test passes when no write to any register occurs during the observed window before any LL function is called.

requirements.statement: When the caller invokes LL_CRC_Read_IDR with a valid CRC peripheral instance, the CRC LL driver shall not wait on any status flag of the CRC peripheral.
requirements.verification: The test invokes LL_CRC_Read_IDR with a valid peripheral instance and times the call; the test passes when the call returns without blocking on a status flag.

requirements.statement: When the caller invokes LL_CRC_Read_IDR with a valid CRC peripheral instance, the CRC LL driver shall not return an error code for the valid accessible call.
requirements.verification: The test invokes LL_CRC_Read_IDR with a valid peripheral instance and a readable register state; the test passes when no error value is returned.

requirements.statement: When the caller invokes LL_CRC_Write_IDR with a valid CRC peripheral instance, the CRC LL driver shall change only the IDR field of CRC_IDR and no other field of the register.
requirements.verification: The test invokes LL_CRC_Write_IDR with a known 32-bit argument; the test passes when only the IDR field of CRC_IDR is modified and no other register field changes.
